correctness.rationale: Uniformly small translated convex-triangle intersections have exactly quadratic covariograms, giving exact F(t)=πt²/A−2Pt³/(3A²)+Qt⁴/(8A²). The quartic law is prior work. The genuinely new injectivity follows since H=∑cot(α_i/2)=P²/(4A), J=∑(π−α_i)cotα_i=Q−3. The analytic curvature ratio g''/f'' increases strictly on (0,π), because tan v>v; weighted secant slopes make Jacobian det ∂(H,J)/∂(a,b)>0. For fixed H, ordered chamber is a connected arc and J increases strictly along it; equilateral and isosceles limits are included. Then P,A reconstruct side lengths via tangent-incircle identity. Independent sympy differentiation and numeric sampling corroborated curvature monotonicity, not used as global proof.

originality.rationale: The exact quartic short-distance coefficient is already published and not claimed novel. The new theorem is full injectivity of three local scalar coefficients on ALL triangles; published general polygon coefficient inequality and full-profile/chord-moment/directional-covariogram recognition do not logically imply local three-jet rigidity. Gates (1982) and Gasparyan–Ohanyan older primary full texts were inaccessible, leaving bounded risk of an equivalent specialized criterion.
residual_risks: 1982 Gates article and 2013 Gasparyan–Ohanyan directional-covariogram article were not inspected in full, so hidden equivalent scalar-jet result cannot be ruled out.
No finite-sample statistical inversion or stability uniform at degenerate shapes.
